issues.description: The rule requires TypeScript strict mode to be enabled in the compiler configuration, but it was disabled in tsconfig.app.json

issues.title: Empty lines not filtered in Expected Events textarea
issues.description: In the CustomTriggerFields component, the onChange handler for the Expected Events textarea fails to filter out empty or whitespace-only lines. When users press Enter multiple times or leave blank lines between events, these empty strings are included in the events array sent to the trigger configuration. This will cause backend validation failures or create malformed automation triggers that expect empty event names, leading to automations that never fire correctly.

issues.title: Incorrect field switching in DeploymentStatusTriggerFields breaks trigger data model
issues.description: The DeploymentStatusTriggerFields component incorrectly implements posture-dependent field switching, using 'trigger.after' for Proactive posture and 'trigger.expect' for Reactive posture. While this pattern exists in FlowRunStateTriggerFields where it serves a semantic purpose (states to enter vs. stay in), deployment status triggers don't have this distinction in the backend data model. This causes the selected status to be written to the wrong field when Proactive posture is selected, potentially causing data loss when the form is saved or incorrect trigger behavior. The backend may not recognize 'after' field for deployment status events.

issues.title: parseInt without radix causes NaN values in threshold field
issues.description: In WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields, the threshold input's onChange handler uses `parseInt(e.target.value)` without specifying a radix parameter. When users clear the threshold field, parseInt returns NaN instead of a number, which gets set as the form value. This breaks form validation and can cause runtime errors when the automation is saved. Additionally, parseInt will silently truncate decimal inputs (e.g., 1.5 becomes 1) rather than properly handling invalid input, and without the radix parameter it may misinterpret values with leading zeros as octal numbers in older JavaScript environments.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #19997 - feat(ui-v2): Add trigger form templates

structured_output.summary:
This PR swaps the four "coming soon" placeholders in the automations wizard trigger step for working field components: Deployment status, Work pool status, Work queue status and Custom. Each one copies the structure of the existing `FlowRunStateTriggerFields`: a posture select, a status select or events textarea, a threshold input, and a "Within" input that only shows when posture is Proactive. I checked the hardcoded event names against `src/prefect/server/models/events.py`, which emits `prefect.<kind>.{status.in_kebab_case()}`, and they match.

There are real problems, though. The PR also turns off `strict` in `ui-v2/tsconfig.app.json`, which weakens type checking for the whole app and has nothing to do with this feature. The three status components disagree on how to store the status in Proactive mode. Deployment writes it to `after`, but work pool and work queue always write it to `expect`. That gives the pool and queue versions the opposite meaning when posture is Proactive ("Stays in"). The custom textarea turns blank or trailing lines into `""` entries in `expect`. One threshold input uses `parseInt` while the others use `Number`. The updated tests only check that the posture and threshold controls render, so none of this is caught.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Turning off TypeScript strict mode for the whole app is unrelated to the feature and must be reverted. The work pool and work queue components store the status in the wrong field for Proactive triggers, which would create automations that fire in the wrong situations. Both need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
The automation wizard keeps one react-hook-form instance built from `AutomationWizardSchema`, and its `trigger` is an `EventTriggerSchema` with posture, threshold, within, match, for_each, after and expect. `TriggerStep` shows a template picker. Picking a template resets `trigger` through `getDefaultTriggerForTemplate`, which fills in `match` and `for_each`, and then `TriggerTemplateFields` renders the fields for that template. Before this PR, only `flow-run-state` had a real component.

The PR adds four sibling components that read and write `trigger.*` through `useFormContext`. Each status component turns a single Select choice into a one-element array of event names such as `prefect.work-pool.ready`. The custom component turns newline-separated text into `trigger.expect`. They all reuse `PostureSelect`, and they all copy the threshold/within inputs from `FlowRunStateTriggerFields`.
steps: Start at `trigger-step.tsx`: `TriggerStep` resets `trigger` from `getDefaultTriggerForTemplate(template)` and hands off to `TriggerTemplateFields`.
`TriggerTemplateFields` now switches to the four new components instead of placeholder divs.
Each component renders `PostureSelect`, which writes `trigger.posture` and sets `within` to 30 when you switch to Proactive and it was 0.
The status components write `[eventName]` to `trigger.after` (deployment, Proactive only) or `trigger.expect` (every other case). Note the difference between them.
`CustomTriggerFields` splits the textarea on `\n` and stores the result in `trigger.expect`.
All of them share the threshold input and a conditional within input. The updated `trigger-step.test.tsx` only checks that these render.

findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled for the entire app
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/tsconfig.app.json` line 19, this PR changed `"strict": true` to `"strict": false`. Revert it to `true`. Then run `npm run typecheck` (or `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json`) in `ui-v2` and fix any type errors in the new trigger-step components (`custom-trigger-fields.tsx`, `deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx`, `work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx`, `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx`) locally, using properly typed field names or narrow casts as `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx` does. Do not weaken compiler settings.

findings.title: Work pool and work queue store the status in `expect` even when posture is Proactive
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx` and `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx` (around lines 28-46), the status Select always writes to `trigger.expect`. Proactive triggers need the status in `trigger.after`. Match `deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx` lines 29-31: compute `statusFieldName = posture === 'Proactive' ? 'trigger.after' : 'trigger.expect'` and pass it as the FormField `name`. Also clear the opposite field (`after`/`expect`) when posture changes, for example in `PostureSelect`'s `onValueChange`, so stale values don't stay in the submitted trigger. Add tests that select Proactive, pick a status, and assert which field the value lands in.

findings.title: Custom events textarea writes empty strings into `expect`
findings.body:
The textarea's onChange splits on `\n` and stores the result directly:

::diff{file="ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/custom-trigger-fields.tsx" lines="26-41"}

- `"".split("\n")` is `[""]`, so `lines.length > 0` is always true and the `undefined` branch can never run. Clearing the textarea stores `expect: [""]` instead of nothing. On the server, `expects()` treats an empty `expect` as "match anything", but `[""]` is a pattern that matches no real event. Clearing the field therefore makes a Reactive custom trigger never fire.
- A trailing newline, a blank line between entries, a stray space, or a pasted `\r\n` all end up as junk entries like `""`, `" "` or `"foo\r"`.

Filtering inside onChange isn't enough on its own. This is a controlled textarea that re-renders from `events.join("\n")`, so dropping empty lines would also delete the newline the user just typed. Keep the raw text in local state and normalize it on blur or submit, or normalize in the schema with a `.transform` that trims and filters empty entries and turns an empty array into `undefined`.
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/custom-trigger-fields.tsx` lines 26-41, the textarea stores `e.target.value.split('\n')` directly into `trigger.expect`. Clearing it gives `['']`, which matches no events, and blank or whitespace lines become junk patterns. The `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` check is dead code because split always returns at least one element. Keep the raw textarea text in local component state so the user can still type newlines, and on blur (or before submit) write `text.split(/\r?\n/).map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)` to the form, using `undefined` when the result is empty. Add a unit test for multi-line input, blank lines, and clearing the field.

findings.title: Work pool threshold uses `parseInt`, unlike every other threshold input
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx` line 78, the Threshold input's onChange uses `parseInt(e.target.value)`, which gives NaN on empty input and differs from every other trigger fields component. Change it to `Number(e.target.value)` to match `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx` and the other new components.

findings.title: Tests only check that controls render, not what the new components write
findings.fixPrompt: Add focused unit tests for the new components in `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/`, following `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.test.tsx`. For DeploymentStatus, WorkPoolStatus and WorkQueueStatus: render inside a react-hook-form provider, select a status, and assert `form.getValues('trigger.expect')` (Reactive) or `trigger.after` (Proactive) equals the expected one-element array. Check that the 'Within (seconds)' field shows only for Proactive. For CustomTriggerFields: type multi-line text and assert the resulting `trigger.expect` array, including blank-line and cleared-field cases.

findings.title: Four near-identical components copy the threshold/within block five times
findings.fixPrompt: Refactor the trigger-step components in `ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/`. Extract a shared `ThresholdWithinFields` component (threshold input plus the conditional within input, using `Number()` parsing) from `flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx`. Extract a generic `StatusTriggerFields({ statuses: {value,label}[] })` that picks `trigger.after` or `trigger.expect` based on posture. Rewrite `DeploymentStatusTriggerFields`, `WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields` and `WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields` as thin wrappers that pass their status lists. Keep the existing labels and aria-labels so the tests still pass.

findings.title: Hardcoded status event names match what the backend emits
findings.body:
The PR description asked for this check. `src/prefect/server/models/events.py` emits `prefect.deployment.{status.in_kebab_case()}`, `prefect.work-pool.{status.in_kebab_case()}` and `prefect.work-queue.{status.in_kebab_case()}`. The status enums `READY`, `NOT_READY` and `PAUSED` become `ready`, `not-ready` and `paused`, which matches the constants here exactly. Deployments correctly offer no `paused` option.

::code{file="ui-v2/src/components/automations/automations-wizard/trigger-step/work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx" lines="20-24"}
